sourceCopy.name: Ideal Weight Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Ideal Weight Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Compare four historical weight equations and an adult BMI reference range by height. Free, private, and calculated in your browser.
sourceCopy.intro: Compare four historical height-based reference equations with a separate adult BMI-based weight interval. They can disagree; none defines a personal ideal or goal.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How does this ideal weight calculator work?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Enter height and choose the historical coefficient set to compare Devine, Robinson, Miller and Hamwi estimates. A separate interval converts adult BMI values 18.5–24.9 to weights at that height.
sourceCopy.privacyQuestion: Is my height sent or saved?
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The calculation runs in this browser. The height you enter is not uploaded or saved by this tool.
howTo: Enter adult height in centimeters or inches.
Choose the coefficient set only if you want to view the older sex-specific equations.
Compare the four historical estimates with the separate adult BMI reference interval.

fields.extrapolationNote: Below 5 ft (152.4 cm), the historical equations are mathematical extrapolations beyond their five-foot reference point.
fields.accuracyNote: These historical equations are not individualized health targets or medical advice. Their original coefficients are binary and sex-specific; they may not fit everyone. The BMI interval is a screening reference for adults, not a diagnosis, and BMI does not describe body composition. Not for children, pregnancy, or clinical dosing.

messages.checkInputs: Check the height and coefficient set.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is not available in this browser.

additionalFaqs.question: Is there one correct ideal weight for my height?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. Historical equations produce different estimates, and a BMI-based interval is a separate screening reference. Neither determines a personal goal or accounts for body composition or individual health.

additionalFaqs.question: Why do the male and female equation sets differ?
additionalFaqs.answer: The historical equations use separate binary coefficient sets. They may not be appropriate for everyone; the BMI interval does not use this selection.

additionalFaqs.question: Can I use this for a child or medication dose?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. This page is an educational comparison for adults only. Do not use it to choose a weight goal, diagnose a condition, or calculate medication doses; ask a qualified healthcare professional.
